cim: Faculties of Education in Latin America address how to prepare future teachers for the age of artificial intelligence
cim_eredeti: Faculties of Education in Latin America address how to prepare future teachers for the age of artificial intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
How can future generations of teachers be prepared to teach in contexts where artificial intelligence (AI) is playing an increasingly prominent role? This question brought together 50 representatives of Faculties of Education from across Latin America in a regional round table that examined the decisions teacher education institutions need to make in order to incorporate these technologies critically, ethically and inclusively, while keeping pedagogy and teachers’ professional judgement at the centre.

The event, entitled “Teaching and artificial intelligence: institutional challenges for initial teacher education”, was held on 14 October 2026 and organized by the UNESCO Regional Office in Santiago, together with the Network of Deans of Education of Latin American Universities (REDECANEDU) and the National Council of Deans of Faculties of Education of CRUCH Universities (CONFAUCE, Chile), in collaboration with CodeAI.

The event brought together deans, senior management teams and those responsible for teacher education from different countries in the region. Drawing on institutional experiences from Mexico, Colombia and Chile, participants examined shared challenges and opportunities for cooperation in adapting initial teacher education to the changes that AI is bringing to teaching and learning.

At the opening, Erika Vásquez Salazar, President of REDECANEDU, and Elizabeth Zepeda, President of CONFAUCE, highlighted the importance of strengthening collaboration among Faculties of Education and reviewing teacher education processes in order to harness the opportunities offered by these technologies without deepening educational inequalities.

On behalf of UNESCO, Francisca Díaz, Coordinator of the Regional Teacher Strategy, stressed that the challenge is not limited to teaching how to use technological tools, but involves preparing teachers who are able to understand artificial intelligence critically, recognize its risks and exercise professional autonomy in deciding when and how to integrate it into their teaching practices. In this regard, she highlighted the importance of moving from individual initiatives towards institutional strategies that address areas such as curricula, assessment, academic integrity and the education of those who prepare future teachers.

The keynote presentation was delivered by Felipe Fontecilla of CodeAI, who identified three key decisions for Faculties of Education: integrating AI into curricula; establishing academic integrity criteria that include declaring and justifying its use, alongside the assessment of learning processes; and ensuring the conditions, time and resources needed to strengthen the capacities of teacher educators.

Fontecilla highlighted the importance of distinguishing between the instrumental use of AI tools and the development of AI literacy that enables future teachers to understand how these technologies work, question their outputs and participate actively in their development.

El panel «Voces desde las Facultades de Educación» permitió conocer experiencias de tres instituciones latinoamericanas que están abordando la incorporación de la IA desde distintas perspectivas pedagógicas e institucionales.

Francisco Díaz Estrada, del Tecnológico de Monterrey, en México, presentó iniciativas relacionadas con el aprendizaje personalizado, el desarrollo de entornos institucionales seguros para el uso de la IA, la gobernanza ética y el desarrollo profesional docente. Su intervención destacó la importancia de evaluar los procesos de aprendizaje, fortalecer el pensamiento crítico y proteger la privacidad de los datos.

Desde Colombia, María Isabel Afanador Rodríguez, decana de la Facultad de Educación a Distancia y Virtual de la Institución Universitaria Antonio José Camacho, abordó los desafíos de la IA desde una perspectiva centrada en la formación integral, la equidad y la dimensión humana de la docencia. Planteó que su incorporación debe estar vinculada con el conocimiento pedagógico, la reflexión crítica y el acompañamiento de estudiantes que enfrentan condiciones de desigualdad, resguardando las interacciones humanas esenciales para la educación.

Por su parte, Luis Alejandro Nitrihual Valdebenito, decano de la Facultad de Educación, Ciencias Sociales y Humanidades de la Universidad de La Frontera, en Chile, situó la expansión de la IA en el contexto de las transformaciones que experimentan las universidades y la sociedad. Compartió los avances de su facultad en el rediseño de las carreras de pedagogía, orientado a integrar transversalmente las tecnologías, el juicio pedagógico y ético, la equidad, la inclusión y la interculturalidad.

The exchange made it possible to identify shared challenges among the participating institutions, despite the diversity of their national contexts. These include the need to strengthen institutional leadership, build the capacities of academic teams, and safeguard teachers’ autonomy and professional judgement in the face of the growing use of artificial intelligence.

As a next step, UNESCO Santiago proposed holding a second regional meeting focused on the exchange of concrete experiences that Faculties of Education are already implementing. The proposal aims to share progress, challenges and lessons learned that can contribute to the development of institutional responses and strengthen cooperation among Latin American universities.

This initiative is aligned with the work of the Observatory on Artificial Intelligence in Education for Latin America and the Caribbean, which promotes evidence generation, knowledge exchange and regional cooperation to support a people-centred integration of AI into education systems.

This article is related to the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals.
